evidence: The PR wired parseColumnSelection into runWorkable (diff hunk at workable.go:162) and the CHANGELOG made backlog-specific claims (refused ahead of the staleness warning, --help enumerates) that no test held; the agent added backlog_columns_test.go including an ordering pin on a fixture that really warns.
guidance_note: When a changelog sentence names behavior on a specific surface, write the test for that surface in the same commit as the sentence.

guidance_note: Before committing a negative-case test row, mutate the code under test to emit a wrong value and confirm the row fails.

evidence: The doc said "Two near-misses" while the PR's own reject test lists lane as a fourth field-vocabulary overlap; the agent took the reviewer's first option (drop the quantifier) and named lane, as shown in the ebd81b5 docs diff.
guidance_note: When prose enumerates a set the tests also enumerate, check the prose against the test table before committing and avoid printing a count.

guidance_note: After fixing a vacuous assertion, sweep every assertion added in the same fix for the same vacuity (an empty fixture or a constant that satisfies the check) and mutation-test each one before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the hardcoded nil rels in printBacklogOutput came from the original PR (diff hunk shows the original line), not from ebd81b5's doc-only change. guidance_note: When a changelog entry names behavior on command X, update command X's own section of the reference doc, not just the section of the command where the feature started.

evidence: be758c1 (the F8/F9 fix) wrote in three places that the blocked column always agrees with the 'blocked:' context line, but nonDependencyBlockingReasons excludes OpenDependency, so a row blocked only by a dependency (the very row TestBacklogRendersRelationColumns builds) shows the cell with only a 'depends on:' line. The agent confirmed the split in the code, reworded all three sites, and pinned the split in a test.
guidance_note: When writing prose that claims two outputs agree, check the claim against each blocking reason, including the case the existing regression test already builds.

narrative: Round 0 found four real original-PR defects: missing backlog tests, a vacuous 'stat' assertion, and two doc/changelog misstatements. The F1 fix shipped a second vacuous assertion (F5). The F7 fix threaded relation data into backlog but sourced 'blocked' from dependency edges only, which left the sibling-gate contradiction in place (F8). The F8 fix's prose then overclaimed agreement with the 'blocked:' line (F10). Round 3 existed only because of that drift; rounds 1 and 2 each also held findings that predate any fix.
guidance_observations: The agent mutation-tested its fixes and caught vacuity, but did not apply that check to the accept test it added for F1, which cost the F5 thread.

Each fix to the blocked column wrote stronger agreement claims into CHANGELOG, docs and comments than the code supported. Checking each claim against every readiness reason before pushing would have saved round 3.
All ten responses were the right call; the rounds came from incomplete fixes, not wrong judgments about the findings.
